tldr: Adds DELETE /folders, which deletes many folders for a user in 1 request.
goal: Clients send 1 request per folder, so a bulk delete costs N round trips.

story.heading: Vault adds a bulk folder delete command
story.body: The command deletes the requested folders, then sends a full vault sync push.

story.heading: Entity Framework deletes folders by id list
story.body: Deletes folders by id for PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite. Single-folder delete now calls the same path.

story.heading: Dapper runs bulk delete in one transaction
story.body: Calls Folder_DeleteByIds with a table-valued parameter. Commits once, or rolls back every delete.

story.heading: SQL Server gains a folder delete procedure
story.body: Folder_DeleteByIds deletes folders by id for one user. A migration script adds the procedure.

story.heading: Clients delete many folders in 1 request
story.body: DELETE /folders deletes many folders in 1 call. The VFO1Foundation feature flag gates it.

components.summary: Adds DELETE /folders, which takes a list of folder ids and returns 1 result.
Deletes the requested folders for a user, then pushes a full vault sync.
Deletes folders by id in one SQL Server transaction through a stored procedure.
Deletes folders by id for other databases. Single-folder delete reuses this path.
Adds the Folder_DeleteByIds stored procedure and its migration script.

decisions.title: One request deletes many folders
decisions.why: Clients send 1 request per folder, so a bulk delete costs N round trips and is not atomic.

decisions.title: Delete all requested folders in one transaction
decisions.why: The Dapper repository commits all deletes together. A failure rolls back every folder.

decisions.title: Push a full vault sync after deletion
decisions.why: Deleting a folder re-assigns its ciphers, so clients need a full vault sync.

decisions.title: Cap a request at 500 folders on cloud
decisions.why: The endpoint rejects more than 500 ids, except on self-hosted servers.
